lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: experimental probability

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

items.prompt: A bag has 2 red and 3 blue marbles. What is the theoretical probability of drawing red?

steps: Identify the favorable outcomes and the total possible outcomes.
Write the probability as a reduced fraction, or use it to predict or evaluate a count.

items.prompt: A fair coin is flipped and a 3-section spinner is spun. What is the probability of heads and landing on section 2?

steps: Identify the favorable outcomes and the total possible outcomes.
Write the probability as a reduced fraction, or use it to predict or evaluate a count.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A meal is made by choosing one main dish from 4 options and one side dish from 4 options. How many different meals are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 5-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 23 times in 115 spins. A simulation of 115 spins landed on that section 21 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
An event has a probability of 1/2. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
choices: equally likely to happen or not happen

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 30 times and landed on blue 15 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A bag has 4 red, 5 blue, and 10 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
A fair coin is flipped and a spinner with 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5 is spun. What is the probability of getting heads on the coin and landing on 4 on the spinner?
A meal is made by choosing one main dish from 2 options and one side dish from 5 options. How many different meals are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 10-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 41 times in 410 spins. A simulation of 410 spins landed on that section 46 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
An event has a probability of 1. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
choices: equally likely to happen or not happen
